prerequisites: Previous mathematical knowledge of vector calculus
Derivation and integration of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the concept of wave and know both its mathematical characterization and basic wave phenomena.
Know the basic concepts and laws of electromagnetism and apply them to the analysis of simple electromagnetic situations in vacuum and in material media.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and apply problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the subject.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Electrostatics: Electric charge. Coulomb's Law. Electrostatic field and potential. Charge distributions. Electric dipole. Gauss's Law. Conductors. Capacitors. Electric field energy. Dielectrics.
Electric current: Intensity and density of electric current. Ohm's Law. Resistance. Joule effect. Generators: Electromotive force. Direct current circuits.

Magnetostatics: Magnetic field. Lorentz Law: Magnetic induction. Hall effect. Magnetic force on an electric current. Magnetic field moment on a loop. Biot-Savart Law. Force between currents. Ampere's Theorem. Magnetic field energy. Magnetism in matter.
Time-varying electromagnetic fields: Electromagnetic induction: Faraday-Henry's Law. Self-induction. Maxwell's Equations. RLC circuits. Electrical oscillations.
Oscillations: Free oscillations. Damped oscillations. Forced oscillations.
Waves: Generalities. Mechanical waves: Concept of wave. Wave differential equation. Wave classification. Harmonic waves. Mechanical waves. Wave phenomena. Doppler effect.
Practical 2. Capacitor Charging / Magnetic Field of a Solenoid.
Practical 4. Mechanical Waves / Standing Waves on a String.
teaching_methods: Expository classes (exposition and explanation of theoretical content, exemplification, problem-solving, large group evaluation activities)
Classroom practices/seminars/workshops (problem solving, group work, presentation and defense of problems/works/projects, small group evaluation activities)
Laboratory practices (handling lab equipment, use of simulation software and/or experimental data processing, analysis of results and report writing, very small group evaluation activities)
Non-presential activities (study of theoretical-practical content, problem-solving and report writing, use of virtual platform, self-evaluation activities)

assessment_methods.method: Partial Exam (T2) on subsequent theoretical content
Final Theoretical Exam (ET) (if T1 minimum not met)
Lab work (P1) - submission of practical results

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, the theoretical block is evaluated by two partial exams (T1 and T2) and class participation (PA), with weights 35%, 40%, and 10% respectively, provided a minimum of 5/10 is achieved in T1 and 4/10 in T2. If the T1 minimum is not met, a final theoretical exam (ET) replaces T1 and T2, weighted at 75% with a minimum of 4/10, plus 10% for PA. The practical block consists of lab work (P1, 8%) and a practical exam (P2, 7%), requiring 75% attendance to practical sessions. The final grade is the sum of the theoretical and practical block grades, but if the minimums or attendance are not met, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, the theoretical grade is 75% from a final theoretical exam (ET, minimum 4/10) plus 10% from PA. If practical attendance is below 75%, the practical grade is 15% from a practical exam (P2, minimum 4/10); otherwise, previous practical grades are maintained. The final grade for the extraordinary call is the sum of theoretical and practical grades, capped at 4.0 if minimums or attendance are not met.
